sites.quote: This may be because [RFC1035] originally specified that these unused "Z" flag bits "MUST" be zero.
sites.reason: Section 4.1 explains why proxies drop packets: it describes what RFC 1035 originally specified for the Z bits ("This may be because [RFC1035] originally specified"), and directs no proxy. The obligation it motivates is the next sentence, RFC5625-4.1-1.

sites.quote: Therefore, proxies MUST ignore any unknown DNS flags and proxy those packets as usual.
Proxies MUST forward packets regardless of the presence or absence of compressed labels therein.
[RFC3597] requires that resolvers MUST handle Resource Records (RRs) of unknown type transparently.
sites.reason: Section 4.3 quotes RFC 3597 ("[RFC3597] requires that resolvers MUST handle Resource Records (RRs) of unknown type transparently."); the obligation belongs to RFC 3597. The proxy obligation this document states is the next two sentences, RFC5625-4.3-1 and RFC5625-4.3-2.

sites.quote: All requests and responses MUST be proxied regardless of the values of the QTYPE and QCLASS fields.
Similarly, all responses MUST be proxied regardless of the values of the TYPE and CLASS fields of any Resource Record therein.
Where the required portions of a response would not fit inside that limit, the DNS server MUST set the "TrunCation" (TC) bit in the DNS response header to indicate that truncation has occurred.
If a proxy must unilaterally truncate a response, then the proxy MUST set the TC bit.
Similarly, proxies MUST NOT remove the TC bit from responses.
DNS proxies MUST therefore be prepared to receive and forward queries over TCP.
As per Section 4.1, proxies MUST NOT refuse to proxy such packets.
DNS proxies MUST implement Section 4.7 of [RFC2845] and either forward packets unchanged (as recommended above) or fully implement TSIG.
As per Section 4.3, DNS proxies MUST be capable of proxying packets containing TKEY [RFC2930] Resource Records.

Since no standard exists for a "local" scoped domain name suffix, it is RECOMMENDED that the default value for this option SHOULD be empty, and that this option MUST NOT be sent to clients when no value is configured.
